images.title: Add the exponents, even negative ones
images.purpose: Shows 2 to the power −4 × 2⁷ on a line of exponents: a jump of −4 then a jump of +7 lands on 3, so the product is 2³.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One horizontal integer line of exponents with two curved jump arrows above it.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal line in dark outline with 14 evenly spaced ticks for the integers −5 to 8; only the ticks at 0 and 3 carry numbers below them, every other tick is unlabelled. An amber (#E69F00) curved arrow above the line jumps left from 0 to the tick at −4, labelled −4 above the arrow. A teal (#0072B2) curved arrow above it jumps right from that tick to 3, labelled +7. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot sits on 3 with the label 2³ above it. Under the line, centred, the label −4 + 7 = 3. Exactly 14 ticks, 2 arrows and 1 dot. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiplying powers of the same base adds the exponents, also when one is negative.
images.description: Shows 2 to the power −4 × 2⁷ on a line of exponents: a jump of −4 then a jump of +7 lands on 3, so the product is 2³.
images.context: 2 to the power −4 × 2 to the power 7 = 2 to the power 3; 1/16 × 128 = 8.

image_decisions.why: Jumps on a line of exponents make adding a negative exponent visible.
